messages:
pagerduty-bot: INC0012377 — Redis Cloud (eu-west-1) increased command latency and intermittent SET failures detected for clusters backing rate-limiter and auth-cache. Auto-page on-call. Severity P2. https://status.rediscloud.example/incident/rdc-4902

monitoring-bot: Metrics: redis.set_errors jumped from 0.05% -> 7.4% in 3m, redis.cmd_latency_p99 ~3.8s. rate-limiter 5xx and auth-proxy 500s rising. Traces show blocked SET calls on quota increments and token revocations.

sre-oncall: Acknowledged. Triage start. Which services hit hardest? Any customer-impact reports?

maria: Customer ops: two EU customers reported elevated 429s and delayed token invalidation. Not total outage but user-facing slowness. Drafting status note.

ashwin: From infra: rate-limiter writes counters via Redis INCR. If SET/INCR slow, we fall back to DB writes which amplify I/O. Seeing DB replica lag increase ~25%. Also token revocations that rely on SET for blacklist are queuing up.

eli: Logs: auth-proxy backlog shows redis error: 
```
WARN auth-cache redis-write-fail key=revoked:tok:abcd err=write_timeout after 2500ms
```
Also a few kube liveness restarts on auth-proxy pods due to long blocking calls.

ops-bot: Redis Cloud status indicates "packet loss on peering to subset of nodes in eu-west-1" and engineers investigating. Ticket RDC-99812 opened.

sre-oncall: Immediate mitigations to pursue (parallel):
- Route write-heavy quota traffic to a dedicated fallback Redis pool (regional ded. pool) if available.
- Flip rate-limiter to "optimistic" mode: accept over-limit for short window and queue deltas for async reconcile.
- Throttle writes from non-critical tenants to reduce pressure.
- Enable token-revocation short-circuit: treat revocation as eventual (mark locally) to avoid blocking auth on remote write.

dena: We have a spare dedicated cache in eu-west-2 that can accept a subset of traffic. Need config toggle and traffic steering. I can run canary for 5% of traffic for high QPS customers.

eli: I'll push local in-memory revocation cache toggle to auth-proxy: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/auth-proxy AUTH_LOCAL_REVOKE=true AUTH_LOCAL_TTL=60
kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-proxy --timeout=5m
```

deploy-bot: Rollout started: auth-proxy (2/10 pods updated). Monitoring error rates.

ashwin: I'll prepare rate-limiter feature flag RLM_OPTIMISTIC=true and start canary on one replica. Also adding write-back queue to process deltas to DB in batches.

maria: Posted initial status: "Investigating increased Redis write latencies in EU affecting auth and rate-limiting. Mitigations in progress." Sending targeted msg to impacted accounts.

monitoring-bot: Canary metrics: auth-proxy pods with local revocation TTL see auth 500s drop from 6.2% -> 2.0%. rate-limiter canary shows DB writes down ~22% on that replica.

dena: Steering 5% of high-volume tenant traffic to eu-west-2 dedicated cache via feature-flag routing rule. Command: 
```
./traffic-router set-route --region eu-west-2 --match tenant=high-qps --pct 5
```

ops-bot: Redis Cloud suggests no quick failover; they are pushing network fixes. No ETA. They recommended client-side exponential backoff and reducing concurrent connections.

eli: Increasing client-side timeouts and adding backoff. Patching redis client config: 
```
kubectl set env ds/redis-client REDIS_MAX_RETRIES=3 REDIS_BACKOFF_MS=200
```

ashwin: After optimistic mode on 50% of rate-limiter fleet, write pressure dropped 45% and DB CPU normalized. We need to keep optimistic mode while RDC issues persist.

sre-oncall: Good work. Plan for next hour: finish rolling optimistic mode, continue steering critical tenants to fallback pool, monitor Redis Cloud ticket. If RedisCloud ETA > 1h, consider broader region failover for more tenants.

maria: Sending 30m customer update — include workaround steps for customers experiencing token revocation delays and note mitigation actions.

dena: Canary to eu-west-2 steady. No errors observed on fallback pool. Will increase to 20% after 15m if stable.

ashwin: Redis Cloud updated: investigating peering hardware; applying patch to a subset of nodes. Still no firm ETA.

incident-bot: INC0012377 state -> mitigation_in_progress. Severity remains P2.

eli: Handover: my shift starts now, taking over incident lead. Dena, please finish routing and hand me the rollout summary.

dena: Handoff: optimistic mode on 50% of rate-limiter, auth-proxy local revoke enabled fleetwide within 12m, 5% traffic routed to eu-west-2. Logs and dashboards in #incidents.

ashwin: Action items recorded:
- Ashwin: keep RDC ticket updated with sample slow-keys and traces, push for peering fix prioritization.
- Eli: incident lead, coordinate traffic steering and monitoring.
- Dena: escalate fallback routing if canary stable.
- Maria: customer comms and status page.
- SRE: postmortem to include circuit-breaker for write-heavy flows and regional failover runbook.

maria: Posted customer update. Key metrics: redis.set_errors 1.3% (down from 7.4%), auth 500s 1.8%, rate-limiter 5xx 0.9%. Monitoring continues.

ops-bot: Redis Cloud reports partial improvement on some nodes after network patch; monitoring shows lower retransmits. They will keep changes rolling.

eli: Keeping thread open. If errors fall below 0.5% for 30m, we'll move to monitoring state. Otherwise escalate. Thanks team.

participants: pagerduty-bot, monitoring-bot, sre-oncall, ashwin, eli, maria, dena, deploy-bot, ops-bot, incident-bot
